content_units: Best Fits for a CS Student
Given your priorities —   portability, battery, coding performance, occasional gaming, value   — the best overall choice is:
1. Acer Swift Go 14
- Best balance of   light weight, good battery, solid coding performance, and price  .
- It stays comfortably under budget and is the most practical all-rounder.
2. MacBook Air 13 M3
- Best for   portability + battery + excellent general development performance  .
- Ranked second only because it is   over your $1,200 budget   and weaker for gaming.
3. Lenovo Legion Slim 5 14
- Best for   gaming by far   and still strong for coding.
- Ranked third because it loses badly on your top two priorities:   weight and battery life  .
Laptop Ranking and Tradeoffs
Rank   Laptop   Weight   Battery   Coding Performance   Gaming   Price   Best For
1   Acer Swift Go 14   1.3 kg   12 hr claimed   Strong for CS coursework   Light gaming only   $899   Best overall balance
2   MacBook Air 13 M3   1.24 kg   15 hr claimed   Excellent   Limited/moderate game support   $1,299   Premium portability and battery
3   Lenovo Legion Slim 5 14   1.75 kg   7 hr claimed   Very strong   Excellent   $1,199   Gaming-first choice
Why this ranking fits your priorities
1) Acer Swift Go 14 — Best overall
-   Portability:   Very good at   1.3 kg  , nearly as light as the MacBook.
-   Battery:     12-hour claimed   is strong for classes, labs, and library use.
-   Coding:   Core Ultra 5 + 16GB RAM is plenty for IDEs, browser tabs, Docker/light VMs, and programming coursework.
-   Gaming:   Fine for   light gaming  , but not ideal for demanding AAA titles.
-   Value:   At   $899  , it gives the best price-to-usability ratio here.
Main tradeoff:
You give up serious gaming power and some premium battery efficiency compared with the MacBook.
2) MacBook Air 13 M3 — Best premium student laptop, but over budget
-   Portability:   Best-in-class feel, and at   1.24 kg   it is the lightest option.
-   Battery:     15-hour claimed   is the strongest here.
-   Coding:   Excellent for programming, especially for general CS work, terminal use, web dev, app dev, and long unplugged sessions.
-   Gaming:   The weak point relative to the Lenovo. Some games run well, but overall game compatibility and performance are more limited.
-   Value:   Strong laptop, but   $1,299 exceeds your stated budget  .
Main tradeoff:
You get the best portability and battery, but pay more and accept weaker gaming flexibility.
3) Lenovo Legion Slim 5 14 — Best gaming machine, weakest fit for your priorities
-   Portability:   Still portable for a gaming laptop, but   1.75 kg   is noticeably heavier.
-   Battery:     7-hour claimed   is much weaker than the other two.
-   Coding:   Ryzen 7 + 16GB RAM is excellent for compilers, multitasking, heavy projects, and dev tools.
-   Gaming:     RTX 4060   makes this the only option here that is truly strong for modern gaming.
-   Value:   At   $1,199  , it is fair value if gaming matters a lot.
Main tradeoff:
You pay with extra weight and much worse battery to get gaming performance you only need occasionally.
Recommendation by Student Use Case
Choose the Acer Swift Go 14 if you want the smartest buy.
- Best match for your full priority list
- Easy to carry daily
- Good enough battery for campus use
- Strong value at $899
Choose the MacBook Air 13 M3 if you can stretch the budget and gaming is truly secondary.
- Best battery and portability
- Excellent coding experience
- Not the best value under your budget constraint
Choose the Lenovo Legion Slim 5 14 only if gaming matters much more than “occasional.”
- Great if you want one machine for school and serious gaming
- Worse fit for all-day carry and unplugged use
Budget Context
A small context note: the ranking assumes your   $1,200 budget is a real limit  , so the MacBook is treated as a premium stretch option rather than the default winner.
